subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should every state-changing Gateway HTTP request using ambient browser authority, including trusted-proxy identity, be rejected unless its browser origin passes the configured origin policy, while explicit bearer-authenticated native clients remain unaffected?
rationale: The issue does not identify a working exploit, but the correct boundary affects trusted-proxy deployments and a broad unconditional guard could break supported non-browser clients; security-owner intent is required before changing the shared HTTP pipeline.

options.title: Audit and centralize the guard
options.body: Map all state-changing HTTP routes and add one browser-origin enforcement seam for ambient-auth requests, with regression coverage for trusted-proxy, bearer, native, and loopback clients.

options.title: Keep route-specific enforcement
options.body: Retain per-route origin guards and document which HTTP surfaces require them, adding coverage only where the audit finds an actual gap.

options.title: Close after negative audit
options.body: Close as non-reproducible only if the route and authentication matrix proves that current browser-capable state-changing handlers already reject forged cross-origin requests.

recommendation.title: Audit and centralize the guard
recommendation.body: Map all state-changing HTTP routes and add one browser-origin enforcement seam for ambient-auth requests, with regression coverage for trusted-proxy, bearer, native, and loopback clients.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work shows direct involvement in balancing Gateway HTTP origin hardening against legitimate loopback client compatibility.
